title: Normalized ordinary tensor and unit for constant scalar restriction
statement:
Let $(C,J)$ be a site small in the coefficient universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], with exact abelian sheafification and the sheafified tensor structures [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Let $B$ be a commutative ring, $B^{\mathrm{pre}}$ its constant presheaf, $R=\underline B$ its ring sheafification, and $\iota:B^{\mathrm{pre}}\to R$ its unit [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Write $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ for sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Sh}(C,\operatorname{Mod}_B)$. Let $F:\mathcal M\to\mathcal A$ be the actual constant-section restriction [def-sfb-constant-ring-module-restriction], and let $G$ extend the scalar action uniquely on the unchanged abelian sheaf. On $\mathcal M$ use the sheafified balanced tensor $\otimes_R$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with unit $R$ and the symmetric monoidal constraints induced by those of $R(U)$-modules [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]; on $\mathcal A$ use sheafified objectwise $\otimes_B$, whose unit $\mathbf1_{\mathcal A}$ is the module sheafification of $B^{\mathrm{pre}}$.
Then $F,G$ are additive exact quasi-inverse equivalences. There are natural inverse isomorphisms
$$c_{M,N}:F(M\otimes_RN)\xrightarrow{\sim}FM\otimes_BFN,\qquad u:FR\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf1_{\mathcal A}.$$
For every site object and local sections $m,n$, $c_{M,N}$ and its inverse send the corresponding sheafified pure tensor to the same pure tensor. If $\eta_B:B^{\mathrm{pre}}\to\mathbf1_{\mathcal A}$ is the module-sheafification unit, then $u(\iota(b))=\eta_B(b)$ for every local constant scalar $b$. The comparisons respect the associators, both unitors, and symmetries of the two specified tensors, so their inverses define a strong symmetric monoidal structure [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] on $F$; $G$ has the inverse comparisons. All assertions hold also for the zero ring and the empty site, without a terminal object or enough points.

source.place: Tag 0GMW, lemma-sheafification-tensor, bilinear-map hint and adjacent tensor constraints; agent-written normalized constant-presheaf specialization including the ordinary unit.

proof.text: Retain the existing additive exact equivalence: restriction across constantCommuteCompose is an equivalence by explicit componentwise cancellation, and the constant-ring restriction is the equivalence of [lem-cbc-constant-ring-module-sheaves]. Exactness follows from preservation of limits and colimits by equivalences [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits].

On module presheaves use the existing PresheafOfModules.restrictScalars lax tensorator and compose it with the constant-module-presheaf-to-functor identification. The latter has identity component tensorators; its coherence is the sectionwise associator and unitor equations. The sectionwise ModuleCat.restrictScalars braiding makes this composite lax braided. Its tensorator sends each B-pure tensor to the corresponding R-pure tensor; its unit is the scalar unit. Naturality and all coherence equations are the sectionwise restriction-of-scalars equations. Compose with the lax braided inclusion of module sheaves (the right adjoint of braided monoidal module sheafification), and with braided monoidal fixed-coefficient sheafification [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. The sheafification counit gives a natural isomorphism of this composite with the literal restriction. Transport its lax braided structure across that isomorphism. The adjunction unit, counit and triangle identity show that the original underlying-presheaf identification is monoidal. Its tensor and unit equations give precisely the required pure-tensor and constant-scalar formulas.

A restriction-compatible B-bilinear pairing between underlying restricted module sheaves is R-bilinear. For a scalar r, use the covering image sieve of the locally surjective scalar unit to write each restriction of r as a constant scalar. On this cover the desired scalar equation is B-linearity and compatibility with restrictions. Separatedness gives it globally, in both variables. Transport the fixed pure pairing through the inverse of the equivalence counit at FM tensor_B FN. Its target is the inverse-equivalence image of that fixed tensor. Upgrade it by this local argument and extend the R-bilinear pairing through the bilinear universal property [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal], using the existing independent-universe specialization in CochainInverseComparison. The universal property uniquely determines the chosen map by its values on pure tensors. Apply F and the counit to obtain the inverse comparison. Both composites fix pure tensors; the tensor and sheafification universal properties prove they are identities.

The unit map is invertible without a separate construction. Choose X with FX isomorphic to the fixed tensor unit. Lax left unitality and invertibility of the tensorator imply that tensoring the unit map on the right by FX is invertible. This tensor functor is isomorphic to the identity and reflects isomorphisms, proving the unit map invertible. Promote the constructed lax braided structure to braided monoidality. The tensor and unit inverse identities give the required formulas for the inverse comparisons. The inverse equivalence inherits the inverse monoidal structure. Every argument uses covering sieves and universal properties and applies unchanged to the zero ring and empty site.

proof_origin.place: Tags 03CY and 0GMW, bilinear universal property and constant-presheaf specialization. U9: lax braided structure by composition and transport; local scalar descent constructs the inverse tensorator; lax unitality and essential surjectivity prove unit invertibility.

Step 1 builds G from the interface's unique compatible action, using that the unit of the already-sheaf H is invertible. Step 3 shows F(Q^#) has the fixed-B sheafification universal property. Step 4 applies bilinear extension with O=B^pre and H=GV, then the Bilin bijection gives a_{M,N}. Step 5 builds d and checks both inverse equations through the universal properties. Step 6 identifies the unit through the underlying-set sheafifications, so u(iota(b))=eta_B(b). Step 7 gets local lifts from the sieve-form epi leaf. Step 9 checks every equation on generators with the orientation e:1->F1, mu:FX(x)FY->F(X(x)Y). Edge cases B=0 and the empty site are handled.
